title: Introduction to New Features in CLO7.0
description: The latest version of CLO7.0 has been officially released! This video introduces the brand-new features in the new version! Detailed instructional guidance—make sure to watch carefully!!
transcript:
Hello everyone, I am Cloud Eva. Today, my colleague Andy and I will be live streaming the new features of version 7.0.  
Now, let's start our live stream.  
What you see is our live stream introduction. Today, we will cover the following five aspects.  
First, let's look at the main updates.  
Second, we will introduce the interface optimization updates to everyone.  
There is also a mode update.  
We will also discuss the optimization of secondary tools and function improvements.  
Without further ado, let's begin today's 3D journey together.  

Let's start with the first main update content.  
For the main update, we divide it into two modules to introduce to everyone.  
The first module is the main update.  
The second module is the pattern color API.  
The second module also includes the parameterized production version.  

Let's first look at this PPT slide.  
After the version update, we can actually connect through the API and the color library.  
We can use the latest color blocks updated previously for design.  
In the lower right corner of the window under the color board,  
we can click this small downward arrow to switch to a different color board of various materials for selection and viewing.  
Due to copyright reasons, the color board cannot be saved;  
it can only be used in the Cloud.  

Next, let's look at the function update of the second module: the parameterized production version.  
This function helps our designers set size and specification parameters to create a basic version.  
We can open the parameterized version editor in the main menu editor.  
In the dialog box, we can create a basic version at the top.  
Below, you can see some of our settings for size and specifications.  
In the upper right corner, there are two options:  
One is Symmetrical.  
By selecting this, we can create two fully symmetrical versions that are linked.  
If we select the Left-Right Symmetrical version,  
this setting generates a left-right symmetrical linked version.  
Now, we can set the front to symmetrical,  
and set the back to left-right symmetrical.  
If we want to create a symmetrical version,  
we need to select the button here,  
then enter a certain value,  
and then complete the creation.  

Here, I will review the process of entering values.  
Let's look at these pattern sizes together.  
Here, I will show you the pattern sizes for the front, back, and sleeve.  
After entering our values,  
you can check if any adjustments are needed.  
There are also symmetrical settings for the front and back.  
After completing these, click Create.  
In the blank space in the 2D window,  
left-click to place the created version.  
We can adjust its placement position accordingly.  
In this way, our parameterized version is created.  

Next, I will introduce the second part: the functional optimization of the interface.  
We will divide it into the drawing window, the settings menu,  
and the introduction of functions such as support for Chinese display.  
Let's start with the drawing window.  

In the drawing window, located at the upper left of the software, a file folder has been created.  
Using the material resources in our fabric file,  
we can see that in the drawing window, these fabric files also support Chinese display.  
In the parameter editor at the lower right corner of the software,  
we can see that the physical property color list also supports Chinese display.  
This makes it very convenient for everyone to search and use.  

Next, let's introduce the drawing and drawing function.  
This function is used to display drawings in the drawing window.  
In the previous example,  
to open our file folder,  
we need to find the corresponding folder in the drawing window,  
double-click it,  
and then in the lower view window,  
we can view the contents of the folder.  
Now, we only need to left-click the triangle button on the left of the folder,  
and we can view the subfolders inside it.  
This is very convenient.  

If we want to return to the previous folder,  
we can double-click the first folder in the window.  
Now, we can click the triangle button on the left of the folder in the drawing window to view or switch folders.  
It is very convenient.  

Next, let's introduce the optimization of the scene page of the object window.  
Here, we can see version information in the clothing file, and sewing line information.  
First, open a project file.  
Go to the scene page of the object window.  
Select one of the pages.  
Here, we can view all internal line information on this page.  
Selecting one of the internal lines in the 2D or 3D window will highlight it in yellow.  

Now, let's go to the Material folder.  
Using the chain as an example,  
double-click a chain,  
and we can rename it.  
In the property editor,  
we can view its information,  
modify its size,  
and also change its name line information.  

In the environment settings,  
we can adjust the default camera parameters and view.  
We can also find lighting properties in the rendering section under the light source file and adjust them.  
These can all be edited and adjusted in the property editor.  
These changes will be applied to our scene, and we can modify them.  

Now, we can close these files.  

The next feature update we will introduce is the optimization of opening clothing, posture, and size options.  
If there is a virtual model in our 3D page,  
and we open another clothing file whose model size, information, and posture are incompatible with the current model,  
a dialog box will appear when we open it.  
It will prompt us to keep the current virtual model's size and posture,  
or to load the size and posture in the clothing file.  

Choosing the first option keeps the model in the upright posture displayed on the page.  
Choosing the second option loads the model posture information from the clothing file.  
This ensures compatibility between the clothing file and the model's posture information.  

The next update we need to introduce is that we can open the color and material list from the mode to the window display.  
We can find this in the editor in the main menu.  
Open the material list and color editor window.  
You will see that the material list editor and color editor can be displayed side by side with our 2D version window.  

To close the material list editor,  
just click the X in the upper right corner.  
Similarly, we can open the color editor window on the right side of the window.  
We can open the windows we want, such as the rendering window, material list editor, etc.  
This makes it very convenient to find.  

We also want to introduce that in our print and export mode, these can also be displayed this way.  
We can open the material list editor and color editor from the editor.  
This allows the material list editor and color editor to be displayed side by side,  
making it convenient to edit material information.  

Let's switch back to simulation mode.  

After the version update,  
we added the function to set the color of the form.  
We can click the email button on the 3D window to shape it.  
You will see that versions set to shape the frame will display in gray.  
Then, by right-clicking in the blank area, we find the option to hide the display color.  
We can hide this gray color.  
Similarly, we can also display this color by right-clicking in the blank area.  
In the settings,  
under the user interface,  
go to the bottom,  
and click the color block on the right-click of the form block.  
Choose a color you like.  
This way, we can set the color of the form block.  
It is very flexible and user-friendly.  

Next, we will introduce the function update and optimization of the third module: mode.  
We will cover four aspects:  
1. Optimization of the color mode.  
2. Optimization of the print and release mode.  
3. Automatic arrangement of templates in the module.  
4. Animation mode with added female movements.  

Starting with the optimization of the color mode,  
we will introduce six aspects.  
Let's watch the operational demonstration.  

First, open a project file in the main menu.  
Then open the color editor window.  
Here, we can see all color blocks applied in this costume, as well as shrinkage objects such as plants, stickers, lines, zippers, etc.  

First, we introduce that we can drag fabric files directly to the shrinkage chart of a plant to replace the texture.  
Previously, this was not possible;  
we could only drag fabric files to the object window to replace textures.  
Let's use Nylon Light and Thin as an example.  
We drag the Nylon Luminous fabric file to the plant's shrinkage chart to replace the texture.  
We see the texture change in the 3D window.  
Click Update at the upper left to see the color information after the update.  

In the object window,  
click Nylon Light and Thin 3,  
then go to the attribute editor on the right.  
We see that the physical attribute preset still retains Nylon Light and Thin's preset and has not replaced it with Nylon Luminous fabric information.  

Next, in the color window,  
click the shrinkage chart of the object.  
In the attribute editor on the right,  
we see the text corresponding to the object.  
For Nylon Light and Thin 2, in the attribute editor,  
we see its type, texture, color info, and reflection info.  
Here, we can edit without selecting the texture from the object window.  
After selecting the texture, we can edit it.  

Next, we introduce the function to display objects hidden by other objects.  
For example, the front chest sticker uses three different stickers.  
In this project, we added three different stickers.  
Click the display hidden sticker button to show hidden stickers.  
Click again to hide stickers we don't want to display.  

Next, we can delete the object Nylon Light and Thin 2 directly in the color editor.  
Nylon Light and Thin 2 are separated:  
this is the Nylon Light part.  
If you click Confirm, you can delete it from our style.  
Note that after clicking Delete, this object information will be deleted from all colors in the entire project file.  
Only one object info remains in the drag bar on the right side.  

Next, interface optimization updates:  
In the lower right corner, the original List and Viewer have been replaced by a button that now displays details.  
We activate it.  
Now, we can hide style info.  
In this mode, a button at the bottom of the style editor window can be used to switch style modes automatically.  
The style editor window layout has changed accordingly.  

We can save the style image.  
Click Save Image in the upper left and select the style editor window.  
After clicking Confirm, our file name is automatically named after the project file name in the list.  
This makes managing styles very convenient.  
We can rename and save this image.  
Click Save.  
We can view the saved image afterward.  

If we want to save a single flag,  
click Save Picture in the 3D window.  
In the dialog box, the picture name combines the project file name and flag name automatically.  
I won’t go into more detail here.  
If we don’t want to save this picture, click Save to cancel.  

Next, function updates and optimization in flower arrangement mode:  
I will highlight three points.  

1. High-density display of parts.  
2. High-density display of parts (repeated in the original).  
3. High-density display of parts (repeated).  
4. Path to flower arrangement scrolling.  
5. Path to flowers.  
6. Path to flower arrangement.  

You can see the red highlighted line.  
After that, moving one panel out of the layout area will also show in high-density red.  
Adjust the viewing angle.  

In layout settings, you can set the number of clothes.  
Click the button on the right.  
Enter numbers such as two S and one L in the dialog box.  
Click Confirm.  
The quantity is set.  
We can change the line direction to double.  

We also have a function update:  
you can display the layout effect during layout.  
Click Start Layout.  
The interface shows the current layout.  
Click Stop Layout to pause the layout display.  
Click Start again; as layout calculates, images update dynamically.  
Later changes stabilize.  
Click Stop to reduce layout time.  
In the attribute editor, we can check number and volume.  

This concludes the layout update introduction.  

Moving to the third module: automatic layout in the module.  
This is an introduction to the automatic layout function update.  
Open a project file.  
Import required saved documents.  
On the right, click Module.  
Enter module mode.  
Click module preview file.  
Choose the module preset closest to your documents.  
Click Confirm.  
Apply this preset to the project file.  

Now, move the required documents to the gray area.  
Panels in the 3D window are automatically arranged.  
Change panel color to gray for visibility.  
In the model's back view, moving a back panel changes arrangement position accordingly.  
This update makes arranging panels easier.  

Finally, use the automatic sewing function to add sewing lines to this T-shirt.  
In single machine simulation, the virtual model can wear the T-shirt conveniently.  

In the third major mode update, we introduce animation mode with added female movements.  
Due to time constraints, we only show the improved animation.  
You can see the animation is smooth, with natural hand movements.  

The fourth module is about optimization of material tools.  
First, let's look at zippers.  

In the zipper function update,  
when customizing zippers, you can select the mesh for the zipper head and zipper,  
add the YKK metal preset, and adjust zipper length.  

Open a project file with a zipper.  
Select the mesh of the zipper head and zipper at the top of the zipper.  
In the attribute editor on the right, click the plus arrow next to type.  
In the menu, change the type to the mesh of the zipper head and zipper.  
Import the OBJ file for the zipper head and zipper mesh.  

In the preview window, the zipper head and zipper preview will appear.  
Select the mesh for the zipper head; the selected mesh is highlighted in yellow.  
Then select the mesh and switch to zipper.  
Define the zipper mesh.  
After selection, click OK.  
The zipper head and zipper are defined.  

Next, the YKK metal preset:  
Set the zipper head and zipper material to metal.  
In the metal preset, choose silver, gold, copper, etc.  
Design as you prefer.  
Here, I set it to silver.  

Select the zipper.  
In the attribute editor, adjust the zipper length.  
If you want the zipper shorter than the large plate,  
set the length to 1 cm.  
Simulate to see the zipper length change.  

After styling, add a separation line design to the front.  
The zipper remains after adding the separation line design.  
This function wasn’t possible before.  

In 7.0, we added separate zipper and fabric design.  
Select the zipper, go to the attribute editor.  
Adjust zipper shape and size.  
Set zipper width and overall zipper width.  
Changing overall zipper width affects fabric width only, not zipper width.  

After setting zipper width, go to material section.  
Post-update, there are six zipper types in the material library: plastic, nylon, metal, etc.  
We can provide style design.  

Apply a metal zipper to the clothing file.  
Select zipper, set metal material, assign silver YKK metal.  
Apply a pink fabric color similar to Dacheng.  
This completes zipper design.  
Usage is convenient and versatile.  

Now, let’s discuss a functional update involving two options.  
Please change the page type to markup.  

If you are writing, you may need to change the page type.  
Markup has four functions.  
Open a group of words.  
In this group, I used a board to make a shoulder strap.  

Previously, we needed to export the board as OBJ and import it into the slot.  
Now, we can convert the board directly into a component.  

Operation method:  
In the 3D window, right-click the shoulder strap board.  
Select Convert to OBJ.  
After clicking, the OBJ button will appear in the upper right.  
The shoulder strap board disappears from the 2D board window.  
This proves the board successfully converted to a component.  

We can use the glue function to stick the shoulder strap onto the shoulder strap board and adjust its position for design.  

For boards with text, we can also set the text as a component.  
Take the butterfly board as an example.  
Note that the text on the board must be set as a component to ensure text information remains unchanged after conversion.  

In the 3D window, right-click the board, select Convert to Component.  
Check the properties in the editor at the bottom right.  
Adjust the weight of the lower specification.  
Use the glue button to attach this component to the body.  

Next, our component can be closely attached and copied to the symmetrical panel.  
Because shoulder straps are symmetrical, we can copy to the symmetrical panel.  
On the other shoulder strap, add the shoulder strap buckle component.  
For the butterfly board in front, we can copy it first,  
then find Mirror Stick in the right-click menu,  
stick it on the master,  
adjust its position,  
and paste our component on the shoulder strap.  

This concludes the upper specification function update introduction.  

Now, we will open the content of the lower specification.  
Please welcome Cloth’s own 3D technology expert, Andy.  

Hello everyone, I am Andy.  
I will begin the lower specification content.  
I will share my screen with you.  
Can you see it?  
Then I will start.  

I will continue explaining updates and optimizations.  
Let's look at the sticker part first.  
There are three parts here:  
- Adding sticker content to the material window and material list.  
- Press distance.  
- Improving cross-section effect.  

Let's go to the software interface.  
Take this file as an example.  
First, open the material window.  
A new sticker label bar has been added here.  
You can display applied stickers.  
It's like a branch and button, displayed directly in the material window.  

To add new sticker material, click Add in the upper right.  
Then choose to open the sticker in the window.  
The sticker is added to our label bar.  

After adding the sticker, drag it directly to the corresponding label position.  
You can drag multiple times.  
You can also duplicate and paste stickers multiple times.  
Shortcut keys are available here.  

These four stickers come from the same material.  
When adjusting one sticker’s size, the others adjust too.  
Thus, stickers under the same material maintain the same size.  

Stickers can also be checked and calculated in the material list.  
To rank these four stickers, select them all, right-click on a sticker,  
and choose to rank by a certain interval.  
You can rank horizontally or vertically depending on effect needed.  

Here, I choose horizontal.  
Enter the interval in the window, click OK.  
The stickers will be ranked per the interval based on the first sticker.  

The cross-selection effect of stickers is also optimized.  
It can hide unnecessary parts after sticker cross-selection.  

For example, take this file.  
The T-shirt is split left and right with front and back.  
Add a sticker to the front chest.  
After adding, open the other half of the sticker.  
Since the sticker is large, cross-selection happens according to seam relations.  
Some stickers appear on sleeves and back, where they aren’t needed.  
We need to hide these stickers.  

Select the sticker on the sleeve, right-click,  
find Hide Sticker, click it.  
The sleeve sticker is hidden.  
Other unnecessary stickers can be hidden similarly.  
Keep only the complete sticker on the front chest.  

Next, let's look at button tool optimization.  
Add buttons to inner lines.  

This is a joint clothing missing buttons.  
Add a button to the front center line.  
Select the button tool.  
Hover over the inner line or first button position, right-click to open the menu.  
There are two button types: based on the start point and average distribution.  

Choose the start point type.  
Create a button based on the first button.  
The start position locates the first button.  
Look at the distance here — the interval from the first button along the inner line.  
Increase the number; the first button moves left.  
There is a reverse direction below; select it.  
Increasing number moves button in opposite direction.  

The interval is the distance between the first button and the upper or outer line of the panel.  
Increasing number moves button downward; reducing moves it upward.  
This is a Korean-style button.  

After setting, click Confirm to install the button.  

Next, create a button using the move button tool.  
Select the button, press it again,  
apply the button to the symmetrical panel.  
The button is installed.  

For the average distribution type,  
use it on the inner line of a spiral line at the back  
to create decorative buttons.  

Use the adjustment panel tool.  
Select the entire inner line.  
Right-click on any inner line position.  
Choose average distribution in the pop-up window.  

Set the distance to 0 to fill the entire inner line.  
Start interval is the distance between the first button and the inner line endpoint.  
Enter 0.1 here.  
End interval remains unchanged.  
Repeat this a certain number of times.  
Preview the effect and adjust the number.  
Click Confirm.  
The decorative buttons are completed.  

Next, functional optimization of edges with two parts:  
Double edge,  
and creating edges at panel intersections.  

Open a new project file.  
Use the edge tool to add an edge at row intersections.  
Change its material for cloth design.  
Edge type can be set to outside.  

Want edges on both sides of the sleeve?  
Set type to All.  
After selecting, simulation is stable.  
Edges are added to the sleeve.  

Look at the collar part.  
Add an edge at the collar and panel intersection.  
Set edge type to outside.  
Select edge mostly on the right side of the intersection.  
This serves as fascia and exterior.  

Do the same for the wrap design.  
Fast and stable.  
Now, rotate the band to these points.  
This function can also be applied to sleeve openings easily and quickly.  

Next, the fifth part: function optimization.  
Mainly four contents:  
Color switch,  
application of drawing on inner lines or shapes,  
optimization of 2D tools,  
and 3D tools.  

First, color switch function.  
It identifies any color in image textures and lets you select a color to change.  
This avoids color mismatches between CLO and other 2D software.  

Look at the software interface.  
Open a file with three colors.  
Use color switch to adjust each color in the image texture.  

For example, select the first sticker.  
Open the image editor.  
In the right editor bar, select color switch.  
Enter the number of colors in the logo.  
The purple color bar shows all colors.  
Hover on a color; all patterns highlight yellow.  
Click the color to change.  

Choose the replacement color in the color library.  
Click OK to change the color.  
You can match pattern and character colors as you like.  

Once satisfied, click Apply and Close.  
Go to the color editor and click Update.  
You can browse settings and see changes.  

Besides logo colors, fabric pattern colors can also be adjusted.  
To change the third flag’s color, select the pattern image,  
open the pattern editor, select cherry blossom, open color switch.  
Enter 4 colors here.  
Select and adjust each color accordingly.  

Finally, change background color.  
If gray background looks bad, right-click to reset to original white.  
Click Reset or Reset All to restore colors.  
After matching colors, open blur edge and adjust background paper for natural color transition.  
Click Close.  
Update to see the adjusted cherry blossom color in the browser window.  

Next, apply layer balance on inner lines or shapes.  
It extends the layer balance to the tablet’s outline.  

Import a suit needing a fold at the front chest.  
Use the edit panel tool.  
Select the middle inner line.  
Grid width is 4 cm, including upper and lower inner lines.  
So add a fold only on the middle line.  
Enlarge the fold.  
The lower fold does not extend to the suit’s outer line.  

In the element editor, select the extension option.  
Fold extends to the inner line.  
Below extension is direction option.  
Choose fold on top, bottom, or both sides of the inner line.  
Selecting side A places fold on top; side B places fold on bottom.  
Selecting both sides creates folds on both.  

Hello everyone, continuing explanation.  
The fold function applies to overall folds of suits or fur coats.  

Next, 2D functions.  
This video hopefully helps most.  
Five functions:  
1. Antenna rotation.  
2. Find askion value in ILL error data.  
3. Check letter data diary from item manager.  
4. Enter CSV file to influence Plot vis-à-vis IPF file.  

Open a project file.  
Sometimes when operating on a board, such as comparing front and back piece lengths,  
we need to move and rotate the board.  
After, we want to reset its position.  
Select the board, right-click, select Rotate, then Reset.  
The board returns to original position.  

Also, the board has code info.  
To export code info to an IOL file, click Export DXF in File, name it, and save.  
In export DXF window, choose size format.  
Two options: include IOL file or not.  
Choose not to include IOL file.  
Click OK.  
Open storage folder to see exported DXF and IOL files.  

Next, optimize the password point setup and move function.  
Use the edit password single tool.  
When selecting a point, distance from the other side password point displays.  
While moving the point, right-click and enter distance from the other side password point to confirm.  
This completes the default movement of each password point.  

When moving password points:  
Hold Shift to move points horizontally or vertically.  
Hold Ctrl to move points along cut lines.  

This optimization allows flexible password entry, not relying solely on the attribute generator.  

Next, improvement of the POM tool.  
It allows importing a CSV file containing points as a POM model without renaming points every time.  

First, create a CSV file.  
In the object window, type POM, enter common clothing points, and reference codes used by the company.  
After completion, click Save and name it.  
Open the path file to see the created CSV file.  

To apply the CSV file, use this file as example.  
Open POM; you’ll see a new POM.  
Import the CSV file into the project.  
Select and open it; your generated POM displays.  

To apply an existing POM to a new name, select the reference POM.  
In the 2D window, display kara black (front middle field).  
Click the application button at the back; the measurement value moves accordingly, showing correspondence of measurement and name.  

Next, select the back middle field, use the measurement point tool to create a measurement point.  
The measurement value appears at the corresponding location.  

To create a measurement point for a curve line, e.g., Xushan Lake, select its name, use the hook and loop tool to select the line,  
right-click to set it as a measurement point.  
The measurement value is added accordingly.  

Finally, delete any excess, non-applicable measurement points.  
This completes the process.  

Next, optimization of the 3D tool.  
Three parts:  
- Matching curve and 3D panel position.  
- Style picture rendering button.  
- Virtual model moving together with costume.  

Open the software.  
Use this file as an example.  
Import a left-hand embroidered piece.  
Choose to add or confirm type.  
Arrange panels, sew, and simulate.  

After simulation stabilizes, right-click the sleeve panel, select spherical panel and example line.  
In the 3D window, the right sleeve position is copied.  
We can simulate it directly.  
This enables quick 3D sleeve simulation with left-right symmetry.  

Mirror extension can also duplicate positions.  
Operate mirror extension copy.  
Positions are copied.  
Since left and right sleeves are not linked, the right sleeve is not connected to the seam line.  

Set left and right sleeves as linked symmetrical sheets.  
The sheets connect to the seam line.  
Select and click.  
The seam line appears.  
Simulate.  

Next, optimize model image rendering.  
Model image rendering can now render buttons and buttonholes.  
Open model image rendering and enlarge.  
You see rendering on buttons and eyes.  
Seam line thickness adjusts by changing seam line size.  
This is the model image rendering function optimization.  

Finally, optimize moving costume and virtual model together.  
Add a costume model in the background array.  
Move model and costume to the right position.  
Import costume and model.  
Select type to increase.  
Click model, then the button on the right.  
Select virtual model and costume.  
Both are selected; positioning ball appears.  
Move the ball to freely move virtual model and costume.  

After placement, import another costume model.  
Use right button and positioning ball to move virtual model.  
Adjust angle during movement for ease.  
After moving, rotate model with positioning ball.  
When done, the final effect looks like this.  

All new functions have now been introduced.  
Thank you for watching.

chunks.title: Introduction to New Features in CLO7.0
chunks.content: # Introduction to New Features in CLO 7.0 This document details the new features and optimizations introduced in CLO version 7.0, focusing on API integrations, interface enhancements, mode updates, material tools, specification workflows, and 3D simulation improvements. It covers technical functions such as parameterized production, color and pattern APIs, automatic layout, zipper customization, sticker management, button tools, edge creation, 2D/3D tool optimizations, and animation enhancements. --- ## Main Updates: API Integration and Parameterized Production This section explains the main updates in CLO 7.0 including the Pattern Color API integration and the parameterized production version editor used for setting size and specification parameters in designs. ### Pattern Color API and Color Board Integration - CLO 7.0 connects via API to the color library, enabling usage of the latest color blocks. - In the color board window, users can switch between different material color boards via a dropdown arrow. - Due to copyright restrictions, color boards cannot be saved locally and are only accessible in the cloud. ### Parameterized Production Version Editor - Accessible through the main menu editor, this feature allows designers to create basic versions by setting size and specification parameters. - Symmetry options include: - **Symmetrical**: Creates two fully linked symmetrical versions. - **Left-Right Symmetrical**: Links versions with left-right symmetry. - Users can assign symmetry settings independently for front and back patterns. - Versions are created by entering size values for pattern parts (front, back, sleeve), then clicking "Create." - The new version is placed by left-clicking in the 2D window and can be repositioned as needed. --- ## Interface Optimization: Drawing Window, Settings, and Language Support This section covers improvements in the interface for better usability, including enhanced drawing window navigation, Chinese language support, and scene page information. ### Drawing Window Enhancements - Zipper head and body materials can be set to metal with presets such as silver, gold, and copper. - Zipper length adjustable in attribute editor (e.g., setting to 1 cm for short zippers). - Simulations update zipper length accordingly. ### Separation Line Design and Zipper Width Settings - Zipper and fabric designs can now be separated. - Users adjust zipper shape, size, and width independently. - Changing overall zipper width affects fabric width only, not zipper width. - Six zipper types available in the material library (plastic, nylon, metal, etc.). - Example: Applying silver YKK metal zipper with pink fabric color for style design. --- ## Specification Functions: Markup Page and Component Conversion This section covers the markup page type and component conversion for boards and text elements, enabling streamlined design workflows. ### Markup Page Functions - Markup page type offers four main functions, including component conversion. - Boards such as shoulder straps can be converted directly into components, eliminating the need for exporting/importing OBJ files. ### Component Conversion Workflow - Right-click board in 3D window, select "Convert to OBJ" or "Convert to Component." - Converted components disappear from the 2D board window, confirming successful conversion. - Glue function sticks components onto corresponding boards or body parts. - Components support symmetrical copying and mirroring for efficient design. - Text on boards must be components to preserve text info after conversion. --- ## Lower Specification Updates: Stickers, Buttons, Edges, and Function Optimizations Andy introduces detailed improvements in stickers, button tools, edge creation, and various functional optimizations. ### Sticker Management Enhancements - Stickers added to the material window and material list with a dedicated sticker label bar. - Users add stickers via an "Add" button and drag them to label positions. - Multiple stickers from the same material are linked to maintain consistent sizes. - Stickers can be ranked horizontally or vertically with adjustable intervals. - Cross-selection effects optimized to hide unnecessary parts after sticker overlap. - Unwanted stickers can be hidden individually. ### Button Tool Improvements - Buttons can be added to inner lines with two placement types: - **Start Point**: Positions first button at a specified distance with options for direction reversal. - **Average Distribution**: Distributes buttons evenly along an inner line for decorative purposes. - Supports symmetrical panel application. - Interface supports precise distance and interval adjustments for button placement. ### Edge Creation and Optimization - Edges can be added at panel intersections using the edge tool. - Edge types include "Outside" and "All" for double edges on sleeves or collars.
